draft: Hi Felix, here's the quick breakdown: General splits your document into fixed-size segments with some overlap -- good as a default for most content. Parent-Child embeds a smaller child chunk for matching but returns its larger parent chunk to the model, which helps when you want tight retrieval matches but fuller context in the answer. Q&A auto-generates question/answer pairs from your source text, which works well for FAQ-style documents. For a general product manual like yours, I'd start with General chunking and switch to Parent-Child if you notice answers feel like they're missing surrounding context.

draft: Hi Lena, it matters mainly for cost and retrieval quality. Economical indexing is keyword-based, free, and doesn't count against your plan's Knowledge Data Storage quota. High Quality indexing uses vector embeddings through your workspace's embedding model, which generally gives better semantic retrieval, but it does consume your Knowledge Data Storage allowance and will stop accepting new documents once that quota is full. If you're on Sandbox or Professional and expect a large knowledge base, keep an eye on your storage usage if you choose High Quality.

draft: Hi Felix, two settings on the retrieval node control that: top_k sets the maximum number of chunks returned, and the score threshold (if enabled) discards any chunk scoring below that cutoff even if it would otherwise be within top_k. If you're seeing too much context, try lowering top_k or raising the score threshold; if you're seeing almost nothing back, your threshold may be set too high for how your embeddings are scoring, or the query simply isn't matching much in the dataset. You can use Hit Testing on the dataset to try different queries and see the actual scores before tuning further.
